_readme: The /onboard-new-client playbook as a chain definition, so the sequence survives a session ending halfway through it. The prose playbook remains the authority on what each step means and why it is ordered this way — this file only carries the sequence, the decision points, and which steps must not be advanced past silently.
name: onboard-new-client
description: Stand up the design-system foundation of a new client project or greenfield area.

steps.purpose: Produce the brand-voice document, ingesting an existing brand book if the client has one.
steps.decisionPoint: Does a brand document already exist, or does the voice need reverse-engineering from existing copy (or drafting fresh)?
steps.checkpointReason: The skill requires attribute-by-attribute sign-off and never accepts a draft wholesale. Advancing past it automatically would break the contract of the skill being composed.

steps.purpose: Reverse-engineer the design and flows documents from the existing codebase, or scaffold them if the codebase is new too.
steps.decisionPoint: Is this a zero-docs project? A project that already has a design-system doc suite skips this entirely.
steps.skipIf: The project already has design and flows documents.
steps.checkpointReason: Generating a doc suite over one that already exists is destructive in a way nothing downstream would notice.

steps.purpose: Establish motion conventions from existing tokens and usage, and haptic/sound conventions from scratch.
steps.decisionPoint: Haptics and sound are greenfield on most projects — ask rather than assuming the defaults.
steps.checkpointReason: Same per-attribute sign-off requirement as brand voice.

steps.purpose: Scaffold the first real screen, now that voice and motion specs exist to draft against.
Record where the project starts, so later runs show direction of travel rather than a number with nothing to compare against.
